title: Maintaining the P-Trap Water Seal
description: A drain trap relies on a continuous water seal—typically 2 to 4 inches deep—to block harmful sewer gases from entering living spaces. When fixtures go unused for extended periods, this water barrier can evaporate, allowing foul odors and hazardous gases into the building. A quick professional maintenance tip for infrequently used drains, such as floor drains or guest bathrooms, is to periodically top off the water or ensure a functional trap primer is installed. Maintaining this liquid barrier guarantees safe and code-compliant drainage performance.

Maintaining the P-Trap Water Seal

A drain trap relies on a continuous water seal—typically 2 to 4 inches deep—to block harmful sewer gases from entering living spaces. When fixtures go unused for extended periods, this water barrier can evaporate, allowing foul odors and hazardous gases into the building. A quick professional maintenance tip for infrequently used drains, such as floor drains or guest bathrooms, is to periodically top off the water or ensure a functional trap primer is installed. Maintaining this liquid barrier guarantees safe and code-compliant drainage performance.
